Separately, Nominatim also resolves a 'Total Merghem' fuel station on the Cairo-Alexandria desert road at 31.0724021, 29.8316016 and an administrative area 'مرغم' inside Mubarak City at 31.0597180, 29.7873976 -- both in the same general vicinity, corroborating Merghem as a real, several-km-wide named zone along the desert road, roughly Km19-29 per the Alexandria governorate's own Industrial Zones page for 'Merghem Bahari/Qibli Industrial Zone' (مرغم الصناعية بحري وقبلي, bounded by the West Nubariya Drain and Lake Mariout: http://www.alexandria.gov.eg/invest/invest/guide-investors/%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%82-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B5%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%8A%D8%A9/%D9%85%D8%B1%D8%BA%D9%85-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B5%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A8%D8%AD%D8%B1%D9%8A-%D9%88%D9%82%D8%A8%D9%84%D9%8A.html). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the straight-line distance from this centroid to the WDGC point above is 5.87km, which is marginally MORE than the sheet's stated 5.0km pipeline length -- geometrically a real pipe's route length can only be >= the straight-line endpoint distance, so this centroid is very likely slightly too far north; the actual plant almost certainly sits in the SOUTHERN part of the Merghem zone, closer to the Nahda/WDGC side. I am not asserting a more southerly point because I have no source narrowing it further -- that would be fabrication. Treat this coordinate as 'somewhere within a few km of here, biased south' rather than the plant's true location.

prior_passes.notes:
THIRD PASS (2026-07-31). Genuine progress on both endpoints but NOT calling this resolved -- see caveats below and the geometric inconsistency flagged in the end.coord_basis. Did not repeat any dead end logged in the retry2 payload (OSM/Nominatim/GeoNames/Photon name search for WDGC/Nahda/butane/GASCO in the Amreya belt: still zero, confirmed again incidentally while running fresh Overpass queries for zone boundaries; GASCO's own site: still TLS-broken, still fetched insecurely only for text, never cited as a [ref] URL; the earlier 'Merghem' claim for the butane plant: this pass independently re-derives a Merghem siting from GASCO's own current site text, which is a materially different, stronger citation than whatever the earlier pass relied on, so it is not simply resurrecting the same unsupported claim).

WHAT WAS NEW THIS PASS:

1) EIA lead landed a major document: the World Bank publicly discloses EcoConServ's 2019 ESIA for the Raven Natural Gas Pipeline (GASCO client) at https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/271011578389920402/pdf/Environmental-and-Social-Impact-Assessment-for-Raven-Natural-Gas-Pipeline.pdf (EcoConServ's own portfolio at ecoconserv.com/oil-gas/ confirms the same job: 'ESIA, ESDD and RAP Studies for Raven Gas Pipeline 75 km (2018)' -- 70km 30in trunk + 5km 18in branch = 75km total, matching this project family). This document independently confirms the corridor and physical termini in prose (Rasheed Gas company at km0 -> WDGC at km70 for the 30in trunk; a separate 18in/5km branch from near El Omoom Drainage to 'next to the fence of the existing Amreya Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) Company', 500m inside to the end point) -- this is our best-ever textual confirmation that WDGC and 'Amreya LPG Company' are the correct, real, physically-linked endpoints for P6704, independent of the sheet's own (wrong) StartLocation. The ESIA contains route maps (Fig. 3-1 through 3-6, Fig. 4-12) that are not machine-coordinate-extractable by me (image-based PDF) but would let a human digitize the exact route if the PDF is opened directly -- flagging this as a strong lead for a human GIS pass. The ESIA's Table 4-5 air-quality/noise monitoring coordinates (three points) are NOT reliably attributable to specific project components (the document doesn't label which point is which) so I did not use them.

2) Wikimapia (lead 4) succeeded where OSM/Nominatim/GeoNames/Photon all failed -- it is a genuinely separate crowdsourced gazetteer platform and has a real, internally-corroborated cluster of GASCO/WDGC-labeled features (7 independent entries within ~700m, not one isolated tag) at 31.0093571, 29.8429334. I verified this by curling the Wikimapia pages with a Googlebot user-agent (standard fetchers/WebFetch get a JS challenge page) and reading the embedded lat/lon out of the page's own script data, and cross-checked via Wikimapia's public API (api.wikimapia.org place.getnearest) which returned the same cluster plus dozens of other Amreya-belt petrochemical features (SIDPEC, Ethydco, etc.) all in the same ~1km radius, confirming this is indeed the real, single industrial cluster that includes WDGC, not a mislabeled unrelated spot.

3) The Nahda-vs-Merghem confusion from the prior pass is now resolved with an important correction: they are TWO DIFFERENT, several-km-apart named industrial zones along the same Alexandria-Cairo Desert Road (Nahda ~Km36, Merghem ~Km19-29 per Alexandria governorate's own Industrial Zones pages), and geographic evidence (OSM neighbourhood boundaries 'ثان النهضة'/Second Al Nahda vs 'مرغم'/Merghim, ~7km apart) now shows WDGC sits near/within NAHDA (only ~1.9km from the Nahda neighbourhood centroid), while GASCO's own site places the Amerya LPG/butane plant specifically in MERGHEM (~5.9km further north/west). This means the prior pass's rejection of the Merghem claim was investigating the right word but the wrong facility-to-zone pairing; with this pass's corroboration (GASCO's own current site text, read directly, plus two independent OSM boundary polygons and two independent Nominatim hits for 'Merghem' in the same vicinity) the Merghem attribution for the LPG/butane plant now stands on real, if imprecise, sourcing.

4) A Wikimapia node literally named 'LPG plant' (id 14533562, 31.0031961, 29.8423326) sits only ~700m from the WDGC cluster -- I deliberately did NOT use this as the Amreya LPG/butane plant endpoint, because (a) its description is generic ('LPG plant is a oil and gas industry located in Alexandria') with no GASCO/Amerya attribution, (b) it is far too close to WDGC and far from the Merghem zone GASCO's own site names, so it more plausibly represents an on-site LPG unit that is part of WDGC's own processing train (WDGC's Wikipedia/trade-press profile describes it producing LPG as one of its own products) rather than the separate, fenced 'Amreya LPG Company' that receives gas via this project's dedicated 5km pipeline per the ESIA text. Using it would risk collapsing two real, physically 5km-apart facilities into one point.

WHY THIS IS STILL NOT MARKED RESOLVED: the end (Amreya LPG/butane plant) coordinate is a NEIGHBOURHOOD CENTROID, not a facility location -- Merghem is a multi-km-wide official industrial zone (Km19-29 of the desert road), and I have no source that pinpoints GASCO's specific plot within it. Worse, the straight-line distance from the WDGC point to the Merghem centroid (5.87km) is marginally GREATER than the sheet's own stated 5.0km pipeline length, which is a real geometric red flag (a routed pipe's length must be >= the straight-line distance between its ends) -- it strongly suggests the true plant location is in the southern part of the Merghem zone, nearer WDGC, not at the zone's geometric center. I am reporting the centroid anyway (per the task's explicit allowance for adjacency-based, tier-capped-low anchors) rather than guessing a more southerly point, because any further refinement I could offer would not be sourced -- it would be fabrication.

BOTTOM LINE / RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP: this is now a well-defined target for satellite imagery: search within the southern ~third of the Merghem industrial zone (Km19-25ish of the Alexandria-Cairo Desert Road, i.e. the end nearest WDGC/Nahda) for a fenced LPG/butane extraction facility, ideally cross-referenced against the ESIA's own route figures (Fig. 3-6 in the World Bank PDF shows the 18in branch route specifically) if a human opens the PDF directly -- the maps in that document are very likely the single best remaining source and were beyond what I could extract via text-only tools. RouteAccuracy should stay 'low' for both a start and end value if staged; do not treat either point as facility-precise for route drawing without a human confirming against the ESIA figures or satellite imagery.
